title: How to Connect All of Your Wearables to ChatGPT or Claude
summary: Your training data is scattered across devices and apps. Here is how to bring it together so ChatGPT or Claude can actually use it.
body_markdown:
Most athletes do not have a data problem. They have a context problem. A Garmin has the long run, WHOOP has recovery, Oura has sleep, Apple Health has the rest, and the lifting session may live in a note or another app. Ask ChatGPT or Claude what to do next and it starts from whatever you remember to paste into the conversation.


That is fine for a one-off question. It breaks down when you want an AI to account for what you actually trained, how you have been recovering, and what is already on the calendar.


## Why this is harder than it should be


Wearable companies are good at collecting data from their own devices. Their apps are built to explain that data inside their own ecosystem, not to give the AI you prefer a complete, usable training record. Moving data from one dashboard to another does not automatically give an agent permission to understand it or act on it.


There are useful pieces of the stack. Apple Health and Health Connect can centralize data on a phone. Platforms such as Terra make it easier for developers to connect an app to many wearable providers. Those are important pipes, but they are not a personal training workspace that an AI can use to review your week, update a plan, and create the next workout.


## What a useful connection looks like


The goal is not to make every chart from every device appear in a chat window. It is to give your AI the training context it needs: completed and scheduled workouts, your goals, benchmarks, and the connected services that inform your plan. It should also be able to do something with the answer, rather than leave you to copy a workout back into an app.


That is especially useful if you train across strength and endurance. A good recommendation for tomorrow depends on more than the last run. It depends on the heavy lower-body session, the race on the calendar, the sessions you missed, and the device data already connected to your training account.


## Connect once, then use the AI you prefer


HYBRD brings together Garmin, Apple Health, WHOOP, Oura, Fitbit, COROS, Polar, Wahoo, Zwift, and other connected fitness services. Its MCP server now lets ChatGPT, Claude, and other compatible AI clients read and manage those integrations alongside your profile and workouts.


Connect the services you use in HYBRD, then connect your AI once. From there, it can work from the consolidated context you approve and create structured workouts in the same place you track and execute them. Your watch remains your watch; the missing layer is the shared training context between it and your AI.


Setup takes a few minutes. Open the[MCP setup guide](https://www.hybrd.com/mcp) , choose ChatGPT or Claude, sign in, and approve the access you want to share. Then try a prompt such as: *“Review my recent training and connected wearable data, then build this week around my race and two strength sessions.”*
